claim:
Let \(S_1\) be the set of squarefree positive integers and let
\[
\sigma_{-2}(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}d^{-2}.
\]
Then
\[
\overline{\sigma_{-2}(S_1)}
=
\left[1,\frac{54}{5\pi^2}\right]
\cup
\left[\frac{10}{9},\frac{12}{\pi^2}\right]
\cup
\left[\frac54,\frac{27}{2\pi^2}\right]
\cup
\left[\frac{25}{18},\frac{15}{\pi^2}\right],
\]
and these four closed intervals are pairwise disjoint. Thus Defant's restricted-domain connected-component problem has the exact value \(L=4\) at \(k=1\) and \(r=2\).
integrity: The component formula follows from a complete subsum argument in logarithmic coordinates. The exceptional prime transition is handled by an exact rational product, interval separation uses an explicit rigorous lower bound for \(\pi^2\), and finite enumeration is used only as corroboration.
scientific_limitations: The result determines only the restricted-domain point \(k=1,r=2\). It does not characterize all \(r\) yielding four components or all component counts for general \(k\). The proof cites Defant's consecutive-prime ratio lemma; the packaged computation replays its finite range but not the asymptotic prime-gap estimate.
title: Four closure components for the squarefree \(\sigma_{-2}\) range
